extracted.intended_audience: Users and developers of the GAP system (mathematicians, computational algebra programmers)
extracted.subtask_description: Reference-documentation for GAP features: filters, types, integer arithmetic, primality and factorization routines, residue class rings, check digits, and random sources. Specifies semantics, constraints, defaults and recommendations for the associated functions and categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heuristic filters default false and toggled true manually or by implication
rubrics_metrics.description: Filters that express heuristic knowledge (e.g., CanEasilyTestMembership, CanEasilyComputePcgs) do not correspond to a strict mathematical property and their value is false by default and may be changed to true explicitly for an object or via logical implications from other filters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such filters need not be computable for arbitrary GAP objects; they are intended to let methods be enabled when heuristic knowledge applies. Use SetFilterObj or logical implications to set them; ResetFilterObj does not reset implied filters (careful with inconsistencies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction of filter kinds vs categories/properties/representations
rubrics_metrics.description: A filter as described is not a category, property, or representation because its value may change for a given object and it does not describe how an object is constructed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filters are similar to attribute testers but do not refer to attribute values; they are used to require a true value for methods to be applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: NewFilter semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: NewFilter(name[, implied][, rank]) returns a simple filter with given name. The optional implied argument, if given, must be a filter meaning that for each object in the new filter, implied will also be set. The optional rank denotes the incremental rank (default 1). The default value of the new simple filter for each object is false.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the new filter is intended to be set/reset manually for existing objects, using implied may cause trouble; consider NewCategory instead if not intended to be set/reset manually.

rubrics_metrics.name: DeclareFilter semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: DeclareFilter(name[, implied][, rank]) does the same as NewFilter and then binds the result to the global variable name. The variable must previously be writable and is made read-only by this function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use DeclareFilter when you want the filter bound to a global name and protected from reassignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: SetFilterObj behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: SetFilterObj(obj, filter) sets the value of filter (and of all filters implied by filter) for obj to true.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Setting a filter may trigger immediate methods; be aware of side effects when enabling filters on specific objects.

rubrics_metrics.name: ResetFilterObj behavior and caveat
rubrics_metrics.description: ResetFilterObj(obj, filter) sets the value of filter for obj to false. Implied filters of filter are not touched.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Not touching implied filters can create inconsistent situations if applied carelessly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Type formation and equality
rubrics_metrics.description: The type of an object is formed from its family, its filters, and optionally defining data. TypeObj(obj) returns the type object. Two types are equal iff the families are identical, the filters are equal, and, if present, the defining data are equal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Type objects are themselves GAP objects and equality is strict on all three components.

rubrics_metrics.name: DataType for defining data of a type
rubrics_metrics.description: DataType(type) accesses the defining data part of a type. Defining data can be used, for instance, to distinguish cosets Ug of different subgroups U: two cosets mod U and V have the same type only if U = V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Defining data is optional but may be crucial when types need to encode extra structure (like the modulus or subgroup).

rubrics_metrics.name: NewType construction
rubrics_metrics.description: NewType(family, filter[, data]) returns the type given by the family and filter; optional data denotes defining data of the desired type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use NewType to create custom types combining a family, a filter and optional defining data; examples are referenced in other chapters.

rubrics_metrics.name: GAP integers are arbitrary-precision
rubrics_metrics.description: GAP integers are entered as decimal digits optionally with sign; size is only limited by available memory so integers with thousands of digits are supported.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In a few places only small integer values can be used (see INTOBJ_MIN/INTOBJ_MAX).

rubrics_metrics.name: Small integer (immediate integer) limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A small integer n satisfies INTOBJ_MIN ≤ n ≤ INTOBJ_MAX where these bounds are either −2^28..2^28−1 (32-bit) or −2^60..2^60−1 (64-bit); some functions (e.g., ranges) are restricted to small integers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of small-integer restrictions when using operations that require internal immediate representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsInt / IsPosInt categories
rubrics_metrics.description: Every rational integer lies in the category IsInt (a subcategory of IsRat). Every positive integer lies in IsPosInt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these categories for dispatch and method selection that depend on integer sign/type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Int(elm) behavior depends on elm type
rubrics_metrics.description: Int(elm) returns an integer whose meaning depends on type: for rationals it returns the integer part of numerator/denominator quotient; for finite prime field elements it returns the smallest nonnegative integer such that elm = int * One(elm); for decimal-digit strings it returns the integer value; otherwise fail is returned for non-digit strings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: String(elm) can compute string representations; Int on strings fails if non-numeric characters present. Examples illustrate field and string cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random(Integers) default distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Random for integers returns pseudo random integers between −10 and 10 distributed according to a binomial distribution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To get uniformly distributed integers use Random([low..high]) or Random with an explicit range.

rubrics_metrics.name: QuoInt sign and quotient rules
rubrics_metrics.description: QuoInt(n,m) returns the integer part of the quotient. If n and m positive, returns largest q with q*m ≤ n. If signs vary, the absolute value is quotient of absolute values and the sign is product of signs of n and m.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: QuoInt is used by EuclideanQuotient methods; examples show sign behavior.

rubrics_metrics.name: BestQuoInt picks quotient minimizing remainder magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: BestQuoInt(n,m) returns the quotient q such that n - q*m has minimal absolute value; if two quotients tie, picks the one with smaller absolute value.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful when symmetric remainders are desired (closest remainder).

rubrics_metrics.name: RemInt sign and magnitude
rubrics_metrics.description: RemInt(n,m) returns remainder n - m*QuoInt(n,m). The return value has same sign as n and absolute value strictly less than |m|. When both n and m nonnegative it equals n mod m. Division by zero signals an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consistent with QuoInt rules; used by EuclideanRemainder methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: GcdInt conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: GcdInt(m,n) returns the greatest common divisor, never negative. GcdInt(m,0)=AbsInt(m), GcdInt(0,m)=AbsInt(m), and GcdInt(0,0)=0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as the integer method for the general Gcd operation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gcdex returns extended gcd with coefficient bounds and unimodularity
rubrics_metrics.description: Gcdex(m,n) returns record g with gcd and coefficients coeff1,coeff2 such that g.gcd = coeff1*m + coeff2*n, and coeff3,coeff4 with 0 = coeff3*m + coeff4*n. If m,n nonzero, bounds on coeff1 and coeff2 in terms of abs(n)/2*g.gcd and abs(m)/2*g.gcd hold. Coefficients form a unimodular matrix (determinant ±1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special cases for zeros: if m or n zero, coeff3 and coeff4 are set as -n/gcd and m/gcd respectively. Example output shows the returned record.

rubrics_metrics.name: ChineseRem existence condition and range
rubrics_metrics.description: ChineseRem(moduli,residues) returns the unique integer c in [0..Lcm(moduli)-1] matching residues mod each modulus if it exists; otherwise signals an error.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Existence iff residues[i] = residues[k] mod Gcd(moduli[i],moduli[k]) for every pair (i,k). If moduli are pairwise relatively prime, existence is guaranteed (Chinese Remainder Theorem).

rubrics_metrics.name: PowerModInt reduces intermediate results for efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: PowerModInt(r,e,m) computes r^e mod m and reduces intermediate results to be generally faster than computing r^e and reducing afterward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use PowerModInt for large exponents to avoid huge intermediate integers.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimeInt deterministic with caveat for large n
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrimeInt(n) returns false if it can prove n composite and true otherwise. By convention IsPrimeInt(0)=IsPrimeInt(1)=false and IsPrimeInt(-n)=IsPrimeInt(n). It is deterministic but may be a probable-primality test for n>10^18; it will warn when argument is probably prime but not proven.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Algorithm: trial division by primes <1000, strong pseudoprime test base 2, Lucas pseudoprime test w.r.t. smallest quadratic nonresidue. Time roughly proportional to (number of digits)^3. Use IsProbablyPrimeInt when you want the similar calculation without the warning. You can switch off warnings via SetInfoLevel(InfoPrimeInt,0).

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimalityProof format and method
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimalityProof(n) constructs a machine-verifiable proof of primality following BLS75 ideas: a list of witnesses of two kinds: ['F', divisor, base] for Fermat pseudoprimality witnesses and ['L', divisor, discriminant, P] for Lucas pseudoprimality witnesses with an extra check at (n+1)/divisor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to produce a verifiable certificate that a probable prime is actually prime using combined Fermat/Lucas checks.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsPrimePowerInt definition and usage notes
rubrics_metrics.description: IsPrimePowerInt(n) returns true iff n is a prime power: there exists prime p and positive integer i with p^i = n. For negative n, requires negative prime p and odd i. 1 and -1 are not prime powers. Implementation uses SmallestRootInt and a probable-primality test.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Works for both positive and negative integers with the stated conventions; may rely on probable-primality tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: NextPrimeInt / PrevPrimeInt behavior
rubrics_metrics.description: NextPrimeInt(n) returns the smallest prime strictly larger than n; PrevPrimeInt(n) returns the largest prime strictly smaller than n. Both use probable-primality tests internally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show behavior at boundaries and negatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: FactorsInt may return probable primes and has size/time guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: FactorsInt(n) returns a list of factors (product equals n). For |n|≤1 returns [n]. Otherwise result contains probable primes sorted by absolute value; entries positive except possibly first for negative n. FactorsInt guaranteed to find all factors <10^6 and finds most factors <10^10; may fail or error for larger multiple large factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FactorsInt time roughly proportional to square root of second largest prime factor (≈ fourth root of n). For better performance on large factors prefer installing FactInt package and use Factors. Warnings about probable primes can be switched off with SetInfoLevel(InfoPrimeInt,0).

rubrics_metrics.name: FactorsInt RhoTrials parameter and Pollard's Rho limits
rubrics_metrics.description: FactorsInt has a second form FactorsInt(n: RhoTrials := trials) to limit Pollard's Rho attempts (default 8192). Pollard's Rho is fast for factors with ~5–10 decimal digits but becomes inferior to ECM for bigger primes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Pollard's Rho would require many trials, prefer FactInt package (which implements more advanced algorithms).

rubrics_metrics.name: PartialFactorization effort levels and guarantees
rubrics_metrics.description: PartialFactorization(n[, effort]) returns a partial factorization; effort controls intensity from 0..7 with increasing resource use. Guarantees vary by effort: effort=0 tries trial division by primes <100 (factors <10^4 guaranteed prime); effort=1 primes <1000 (factors <10^6 guaranteed); effort=2 adds more primes and perfect power detection (factors <10^6 guaranteed); effort=3 adds Pollard's Rho with RhoTrials=256; effort=4 uses RhoTrials=2048; effort=5 uses RhoTrials=8192 and ensures factors <10^12 are guaranteed prime and all prime factors <10^6 found; effort=6/7 with FactInt loaded do much more (including MPQS omissions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Increasing effort typically multiplies runtime by ~3–10 per step. Use PartialFactorization to get progressive improvement and tuned effort when full factorization is expensive.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrintFactorsInt human-readable output
rubrics_metrics.description: PrintFactorsInt(n) prints the prime factorization of n in human-readable form (e.g., 2^4*3^2*5*7).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful for displaying factorization succinctly; see StringPP for formatted strings.

rubrics_metrics.name: PrimePowersInt returns prime power vector
rubrics_metrics.description: PrimePowersInt(n) returns prime factorization as a flat list [p1,e1,...,pk,ek] with n = p1^e1 * ... * pk^ek; for negative input absolute value used; zero is not allowed. PrimePowersInt(1) returns empty list.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when programmatic access to primes and exponents is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: DivisorsInt returns sorted divisors and errors on zero
rubrics_metrics.description: DivisorsInt(n) returns a sorted list of all divisors of n starting with 1 and ending with n. DivisorsInt(-n)=DivisorsInt(n). Calling DivisorsInt(0) causes an error because divisors of 0 are infinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May call FactorsInt internally; use Sigma and Tau for sum and count of positive divisors respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZmodnZ / ZmodpZ / ZmodpZNC ring semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: ZmodnZ(n) returns a ring isomorphic to integers modulo n. ZmodpZ(p) does the same with p prime and additionally returns a field. ZmodpZNC omits the primality check. Elements correspond to residue classes; Int(x) gives a representative integer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When n is not prime the ring contains whole family of elements; when prime the ring is embedded into finite field elements of characteristic n.

rubrics_metrics.name: ZmodnZObj returns elements by family or by integer representative
rubrics_metrics.description: ZmodnZObj(Fam,r) returns element in Fam whose coset is represented by integer r; ZmodnZObj(r,n) returns element in ZmodnZ(n) represented by r.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Useful to construct or coerce residues into a specific residue-class family or ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: IsZmodnZObj and related categories and distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Categories IsZmodnZObj, IsZmodnZObjNonprime, IsZmodpZObj, IsZmodpZObjSmall, IsZmodpZObjLarge classify elements of Z/nZ with distinctions: prime vs nonprime case and small vs large prime field elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reasons to distinguish prime/nonprime: external representation exists for nonprime, comparison can be residue comparison, and family types differ. Small/large distinction matters for compatibility with internal finite field representation and choice of comparison semantics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Check digit functions behavior and input forms
rubrics_metrics.description: CheckDigitISBN, CheckDigitISBN13, CheckDigitPostalMoneyOrder, CheckDigitUPC compute or check check digits: input may be the full number with check digit (returns true/false) or number without check digit (returns missing digit). Input accepted as integer, string (preserves leading zeros), or sequence of digits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ISBN uses modulo 11 arithmetic with digit 'X' representing the value 10 (text notes representation as 'X'); CheckDigitTestFunction can create arbitrary inner-product based check digit tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: CheckDigitTestFunction creates linear check schemes
rubrics_metrics.description: CheckDigitTestFunction(l,m,f) creates a test function for check digit schemes using inner products with fixed vector f modulo m; strings of length l (including check digit) are tested by dot-product modulo m equalling 0.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned function accepts the number as before and can be used to compute missing check digit or test a full number. Example demonstrates ISBN-like construction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Random source abstraction and interface
rubrics_metrics.description: IsRandomSource is the category for random source objects. RandomSource(cat[,seed]) creates a new random source rs. Random(rs,list) yields a random element of list, Random(rs,low,high) yields a random integer in [low..high]. The choice must depend only on rs (no effect on other random sources). State(rs) returns a copy of current state (or fail if cannot reset). Reset(rs,seed) resets rs to a state described by seed (or uses default seed if omitted) and returns previous state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use independent random sources to make algorithms deterministic by creating a new source with fixed seed. Prefer using State output as seed rather than integer seeds; historical support for integer seeds exists but is discouraged. If a random source cannot be reset, State returns fail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Kinds of random sources and recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Provided kinds: IsMersenneTwister (fast 32-bit Mersenne Twister; period 2^19937−1; 623-dim equidistribution), IsGAPRandomSource (GAP-specific generator producing independent sequences), IsGlobalRandomSource (legacy global additive generator). GlobalMersenneTwister and GlobalRandomSource are predefined globals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Mersenne Twister when possible, especially for generating many large random integers; GlobalMersenneTwister is the default for library methods that don't accept a random source. Do not construct multiple GlobalRandomSource-like generators (they would share global state). Other random source kinds may be provided by packages.

rubrics_metrics.name: RandomSource creation and seed semantics
rubrics_metrics.description: RandomSource(cat[,seed]) creates a new random source of category cat (e.g., IsMersenneTwister). Optional seed specifies initial state; see State/Reset for details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When reproducibility is desired, either Reset with a State output or create the RandomSource with a known seed according to the random source's semantics; prefer using State outputs for portability.
